question: Should packaged OpenClaw updates officially preserve local `dist` edits and offer explicit trusted replay, or should modified installed packages remain unsupported?
rationale: The implementation is defensively engineered, but accepting it creates ongoing update compatibility, support, release-policy, and executable-code security commitments that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Preserve with opt-in replay
options.body: Adopt recovery-bundle capture by default and allow explicit trusted replay after the existing integrity and topology checks.

options.title: Preserve without replay
options.body: Keep recovery bundles and reporting but remove automatic replay so installed-package mutation remains unsupported.

options.title: Reject modified installs
options.body: Decline the new contract and direct users with local modifications to reinstall or maintain a source checkout.

recommendation.title: Preserve with opt-in replay
recommendation.body: Adopt recovery-bundle capture by default and allow explicit trusted replay after the existing integrity and topology checks.
